summary_text: In March 2026, the user placed orders on 16 independent dates, primarily on weekdays (10 dates) and weekends (6 dates). Orders were distributed across morning, afternoon, evening, and night dayparts, with a notable concentration in the afternoon and morning slots. The basket composition varied widely, ranging from narrow, single-category or two-category purchases (e.g., Eggs and Breads; Curd Yogurt and Buttermilk) to broader baskets involving five distinct categories (e.g., Breads, Sugar, Cheese, Butter Margarine, and Tea). Common categories included Breads, Milk, Curd Yogurt, Eggs, and Savouries Namkeens. While Breads appeared frequently across many dates, it was paired with different categories each time (Eggs, Milk, Cheese, Paneer Tofu, Dips Sauces Pastes, etc.), preventing the formation of a stable, repeated category combination pattern. Similarly, Milk and Curd Yogurt appeared on multiple dates but were paired with different items each time. No single category combination or daypart behavior recurred with sufficient frequency to establish a high-confidence stable pattern. Shopping needs inferred are compatible with general breakfast preparation, light snacking, and basic household replenishment, but these are based on isolated observations rather than repeated routines.

Eggs were purchased on 2 independent dates (2026-03-02, 2026-03-29), both times paired with Breads in the morning, suggesting a potential but unconfirmed breakfast routine.

shopping_need_text: The user demonstrates a need for basic breakfast components (Breads, Eggs, Milk, Curd Yogurt), light snacking items (Savouries Namkeens, Chips, Chocolate), and general household staples (Sugar, Tea, Canned Food). The variety of pairings suggests flexible meal preparation rather than a fixed routine.
uncertainty_text: Confidence is low for any specific category combination or routine because no pattern repeats with the same components across multiple independent dates. While individual categories like Breads and Curd Yogurt appear frequently, their companions change each time, preventing the establishment of a stable basket-building pattern.
